questions.question: The _______ dance form originated as a tribal dance in the forests of Odisha in the 18th century and attained the status of a martial art-based dance form in the 19th century.
questions.questionHtml: The _______ dance form originated as a tribal dance in the forests of Odisha in the 18th century and attained the status of a martial art-based dance form in the 19th century.
questions.solution:
• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance form that originated as a tribal dance in the forests of Odisha in the 18th century and in the 19th century it attained the status of martial art-based dance.
  • There are 3 styles of Chhau which are named according to the states in which they are performed, that is, Seraikella Chau of Jharkhand, Mayurbhanj Chau of Odisha, and Purulia Chau of Bengal.
  • The costumes vary among the different styles of Chhau.
  • The dance covers folk, martial, and tribal traditions and is performed on instrumental music mainly on a variety of drums such as Dhumba, Dhol, Dhansa, and Nagara.

questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Padma Bhushan awardee, was a globally renowned dancer of which of the following gharanas of Kathak?
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Padma Bhushan awardee, was a globally renowned dancer of which of the following gharanas of Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kalka-BindadinKey Points

  • Pandit Birju Maharaj was an Indian dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance in India.
  • He was a descendant of the Maharaj family of Kathak dancers, which includes his two uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, and his father and guru, Acchan Maharaj.
  • He was born on 4 February 1938 in Handia and died on 17 January 2022 in Delhi.
  • He was awarded Padma Vibhushan and Filmfare Award for Best Choreography and more.
  • Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance. It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh. The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.

questions.question: Dr.Teejan Bai, a Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awardee is globally recognised for her contribution to which of the following art forms?
questions.questionHtml: Dr.Teejan Bai, a Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awardee is globally recognised for her contribution to which of the following art forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pandavani.

 Key Points

  • Dr. Teejan Bai:-
    • She was born on August 8, 1956, in the village of Ghughara, Chandrapur district of Chhattisgarh, India.
    • She hails from the Gond tribal community, and her family has a rich tradition of Pandavani, a traditional storytelling art form that narrates tales from the epic Mahabharata.
    • Teejan Bai's contributions to Pandavani have been recognized with numerous prestigious awards, including Padma Shri in 1987, Padma Bhushan in 2003, Padma Vibhushan, the 2nd highest civilian award in India, in 2019, and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1995.
  • Pandwani means Pandavwani – that is Panda Katha, a story of Mahabharata. Pandwani is a folk ballad form performed predominantly in Chhattisgarh.

Additional Information

  • Gendi:-
    • It is a lively and energetic dance performed during festivals and celebrations.
    • It is characterized by its acrobatic movements, where dancers balance themselves on two long bamboo poles, performing intricate steps and twirls.
  • Raut Nacha:-
    • It is a dramatic and narrative dance that depicts the story of Lord Krishna and his battles against the evil forces of King Kansa.
    • The dance is performed by men dressed as cowherds, wielding sticks and shields, enacting the scenes of Krishna's bravery and triumph.
  • Jhirliti:-
    • It is a unique and playful dance performed by children during festivals and celebrations.
    • It is characterized by its whimsical and impromptu nature, where children dress up in colorful rags and masks, dancing in circles and performing playful antics.
    • The dance is accompanied by the sounds of clapping, singing, and makeshift instruments, creating a joyful and lighthearted atmosphere.

questions.question: Who is the first classical dancer of foreign origin who was conferred the Padma Shri in 2006 for her contributions to Odissi?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the first classical dancer of foreign origin who was conferred the Padma Shri in 2006 for her contributions to Odissi?

    • She is a master of the Mayurbhanj Chhau, which she studied under the guidance of Guru Hari Nayak.

    • She won the Best Choreography prize at the 43rd National Film Awards in 1995 for Yugant.
    • In 1996, she established the Art Vision Academy, a place for ideas sharing amongst various artistic mediums like theatre, music, dance, and painting.

questions.question: Pandit Gopal Prasad Dubey won the Padma Shri for which form of dance?
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Gopal Prasad Dubey won the Padma Shri for which form of dance?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Chhau.

Key Points

  • Chhau is a traditional Indian dance form that combines martial arts, acrobatics, and storytelling.
  • It is predominantly performed in the eastern states of India, including West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha.
  • The dance is known for its energetic movements and is often performed during festivals and religious occasions.
  • Chhau dance has three main styles: Purulia Chhau of West Bengal, Seraikella Chhau of Jharkhand, and Mayurbhanj Chhau of Odisha.
  • The dancers often wear elaborate masks and costumes to represent different characters, including gods, goddesses, and animals.
  • This dance form has been inscribed in UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in the year 2010.

 Additional Information

  • Kathakali
    • Kathakali is a classical dance form originating from Kerala.
    • It is known for its elaborate costumes, detailed gestures, and well-defined body movements presented in the form of story play.
    • Kathakali performances are typically based on Hindu epics such as the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
  • Bihu
    • Bihu is a folk dance from the state of Assam.
    • It is associated with the Bihu festival, which marks the Assamese New Year and the harvest season.
    • The dance is characterized by quick hand movements, brisk steps, and rhythmic swaying.
  • Sattriya
    • Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam.
    • It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev as a medium for religious teachings.
    • The dance is performed in monasteries called Satras.

questions.question: To which of the following Gharanas did Hindustani Classical Vocalist, Bhimsen Joshi belong?
questions.questionHtml: To which of the following Gharanas did Hindustani Classical Vocalist, Bhimsen Joshi belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kirana Gharana.

Key Points

  • Bhimsen Joshi belonged to the Kirana Gharana, a prominent school of Hindustani classical music.
  • The Kirana Gharana is known for its emphasis on intricate melodic patterns, slow and meditative style, and use of the 'gayaki ang' or singing style.
  • Bhimsen Joshi's music was shaped by the teachings of his guru, Sawai Gandharva, who was also associated with the Kirana Gharana.
  • Joshi's rendition of classical ragas and devotional compositions showcased the aesthetic of the Kirana Gharana.
  • His performances earned him acclaim as one of the greatest vocalists in Indian classical music.
  • His legacy continues to inspire aspiring musicians and enthusiasts of classical music worldwide.

Additional Information

  • Agra Gharana
    • Emerged in the city of Agra, Uttar Pradesh, in medieval Northern India.
    • Established by Haji Sujan Khan, a court musician of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
    • Has significantly impacted Hindustani classical music, particularly vocal styles.
    • Includes Faiyaz Khan, Vilayat Hussain Khan, Khadim Hussain Khan, and Sharafat Hussain Khan.
  • Rampur Sahaswan Gharana
    • Founded in the princely state of Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, in the 19th century.
    • Established by Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan and Ustad Mehboob Khan, court musicians of Rampur.
    • Known for intricate melodic patterns, rhythmic improvisations, and systematic presentation of ragas.
    • Includes Ustad Mushtaq Hussain Khan, Ustad Nissar Hussain Khan, and Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.
  • Gwalior Gharana
    • Emerged in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India.
    • Established by musicians patronized by the Scindia dynasty rulers.
    • Includes Ustad Haddu Khan, Ustad Nathu Khan, Ustad Hassu Khan, and Pandit Vinayak Rao Patwardhan.
    • Profound impact on Hindustani classical music, particularly vocal styles and compositions.

questions.question: Ram Sahay Pandey, a Padma Shri 2022 awardee, is associated with which of the following dance forms of the Bedia community of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.questionHtml: Ram Sahay Pandey, a Padma Shri 2022 awardee, is associated with which of the following dance forms of the Bedia community of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is RaiKey Points 

  • Ram Sahay Pandey was awarded the Padma Shri for his contribution to Bundeli Folk Dance in 2022.
  • Ram Sahay Panday is a Rai dancer from Madhya Pradesh's sagar district.
  • The Rai dance was traditionally associated with the Bedia community.
  • Though he was not the member of the community he devoted his whole life practicing and performing the Rai dance and to secure acceptance and respectability for the dance form.
  • His efforts helped him obtain national and international recognition of Rai dance form.
  • The dance form Raai (or Rai) is basically a folk dance of the Bundelkhand region. 
  • In the year 2022, Govt of India honoured Ram Sahay Panday by conferring the Padma Shri award for his contributions to art.

Additional Information

  • Badhai:
    • Badhai is one of the popular folk dances of Madhya Pradesh, especially in the Bundelkhand region.
    • It is a ceremonial dance, performed on childbirth, marriages or any other get together to celebrate happiness and joy.
    • The musical instruments used are Dhapla, Timki, Lota, Rantula & Algoja.
  • Karma​
    • Khemta and Bhinusari are the two forms of Karma dance.
    • Karma dance is a traditional dance of central and Eastern India annually performed during the karma festival. 
    • It is performed in Jharkhand and its adjacent states of Chhattisgarh, West Orissa and Madhya Pradesh.
    • It is held during the autumn season.
  • Ravala
    • Ravala Dance is a traditional folk dance from the state of Rajasthan, India.
    • It is performed by the Ravala community, which is part of the larger Rajput or Gujjar groups.
    • This dance is a vibrant and energetic form of expression that showcases the rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan
    • The dance is usually performed during festivals and cultural celebrations.

  • Performers of the Rikham Pada dance wear traditional attire and adorn themselves with colorful ornaments.

questions.question: The Manipuri dance of north-eastern India is grown out of the ritual worship of Lord _________ .
questions.questionHtml: The Manipuri dance of north-eastern India is grown out of the ritual worship of Lord _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Krishna.

Key Points

  • Manipuri dance, also known as Jagoi, is one of the major classical dance forms of India, originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
  • This dance form is primarily associated with the Vaishnavism tradition, which worships Lord Krishna.
  • The dance is characterized by its graceful and fluid movements, and it is deeply rooted in the ritualistic and devotional aspects of Vaishnavism.
  • Manipuri dance incorporates elements of Raslila and Thang Ta (martial arts), both of which celebrate the life and stories of Lord Krishna.

Additional Information

  • Vaishnavism
    • Vaishnavism is one of the major traditions within Hinduism, centered around the worship of Vishnu and his avatars, primarily Krishna and Rama.
    • It emphasizes the devotion (bhakti) to Vishnu as the supreme deity and promotes the chanting of holy names and the performance of rituals dedicated to Vishnu.
    • Vaishnavism has a rich tradition of art, music, and dance, with many classical dance forms, including Manipuri, drawing inspiration from its themes and stories.
  • Raslila
    • Raslila is a traditional performance art that narrates the divine love story of Krishna and the gopis (milkmaids) of Vrindavan.
    • It is an important aspect of the Manipuri dance form, showcasing the playful and romantic aspects of Krishna's life.
    • Raslila performances are characterized by their devotional singing, expressive dance, and elaborate costumes.
  • Thang Ta
    • Thang Ta is a traditional martial art form of Manipur, combining armed and unarmed combat techniques.
    • It is often integrated into Manipuri dance performances to depict stories of valor and heroism from Krishna's life.
    • Thang Ta showcases the rich cultural heritage of Manipur and its emphasis on physical fitness, agility, and discipline.

questions.question: Of the following, which is Kumudini Lakhia most famous dancing style?
questions.questionHtml: Of the following, which is Kumudini Lakhia most famous dancing style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathak.

Key Points

  •  Kathak 
    • ​One of the eight primary styles of Indian classical dance is kathak.
    • It is an Uttar Pradesh classical dancing style. The storytellers or itinerant bards known as Kathakars in ancient northern India are often credited as the creators of Kathak.
    • The Vedic Sanskrit words Katha, which means "story," and Kathakar, which means "the one who tells a story" or "to do with stories," are the roots of the word Kathak.
    • Traveling Kathakars used dance, songs, and music to transmit tales from the great epics and ancient mythology. Kathak dancers use intricate footwork, flexible body movements, and, most importantly, expressive face expressions to convey a variety of stories.

Additional Information

  • Kuchipudi 
    • One of the eight principal Indian classical dances is Kuchipudi.
    • It comes from the Andhra Pradesh state of India, specifically the village of Kuchipudi.
    • Kuchipudi was created as a way to worship Krishna, a Hindu deity.
    • Siddhendra Yogi, a gifted poet and visionary who belonged to the Vaishnava sect and had the ability to give some of his visions solid form, created the Kuchipudi style of Yakshagaana in the 17th century.
    • Kuchipudi is renowned for its dynamic storytelling, dramatic characterization, outstanding, rapid dancing, and expressive eye movements.
    • Tandava (the regal, masculine) and Lasya (lyrical graceful and feminine energy) are combined in this dance.
    • Other famous dance forms of Andhra Pradesh include - Vilasini Natyam, Andhra Natyam, Bhamakalpam, Veeranatyam, Dappu, Tappeta Gullu, Lambadi, Dhimsa, Kolattam, Butta Bommalu.
  • ​Sattriya
    • Satriya Nritya is the classical dance form of Assam which represents the Satriya culture, the basis of the religious and cultural fabric of Assam.
    • It is a dance-drama performance art with origins in the Krishna-centered Vaishnavism monasteries of Assam and attributed to the 15th-century Bhakti movement scholar and saint Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev.
    • Dance historian Dr. Sunil Kothari has recently been bestowed with the Madhabdev Award by the Government of Assam for popularising the Sattriya dance.
    • Sattriya was given the status of classical dance in the year 2000 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
  • ​Bharatnatyam
    • Bharatnatyam dance origin can be traced from back to Sadir-the solo dance of temple dancer or devadasis in Tamil Nadu.
    • Bharatnatyam is also known as Dashiattam.
    • Elements of Bharatnatyam:
    • Alarippu-seeking blessing of god with simple dance steps in rhythm.
    • Jatiswaram-Nritta component with devoid expression.
    • Shabdam-dramatic element with expressed words.
    • Varnam-combination of dance and emotion to express a story.
    • Padam-mastery over abhinaya of a spiritual message by the artist.
    • Jawali-Its performed at short love lyrics at a fast tempo.
    • Thillana-It is known as the concluding Stage with pure dance(Nritta).
